text.p: Standard & Poor's rating agency said on Thursday it had cut its senior unsecured and counterparty long-term rating of Selectibanque to BBB from A minus and its short-term rating to A3 from A2.
"At the same time, Selectibanque's ratings have been removed from CreditWatch where they were placed on January 23, 1997," S&P said in a statement.
It added the outlook on the long-term rating was negative.
"This decision reflects the sharp weakening of Selectibanque's financial profile, primarily as a consequence of an aggressive external growth strategy implemented in 1995," S&P said.
"However, Selectibanque's ratings also take into account potential support from its shareholder, the Suez group, should the need arise."
Selectibanque is the banking arm and one of the main subsidiaries of ISM SA, a real estate company that has diversified into commercial property finance, and residually, property development.

Selectibanque itself specialises in real estate financing for French companies, primarily in the form of leasing. The Suez group owns 83 percent of ISM SA, which has itself a controlling stake in Selectibanque.
"Standard & Poor's considers that the Suez group's financial situation should benefit from the significant restructuring that is currently underway," the statement said.
"Though real estate financing is not a business the Suez group is trying to develop, Selectibanque's ratings take into account the support the Suez group could provide in case of need."
S&P said the recent erosion in Selectibanque's financial situation reflected the impact of a highly competitive banking environment and an aggressive external growth strategy launched in 1995.

"This strategy was intended to compensate for the progressive winding down of a lease granted to France Telecom, which represented one third of the bank's consolidated assets at year-end 1994," said S&P.
"In Standard & Poor's view, the assets acquired have raised Selectibanque's risk profile."
